summary: A 1884 pole beacon on the Great Bras d'Or channel, replaced by a 1909 wooden tower; Lauchlin McNeil kept it 1884 to 1927. Discontinued in 1961; restored; ownership disputed.

structures.type: dioptric lantern on a 25-foot pole beside a white shed
square pyramidal wood tower with lantern and gallery

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends; Rowlett). The trail to the light descends through private property (Rowlett). Lighthouse Friends reports a 'No Lighthouse Access' sign in 2020.

facts.agency: Disputed: Boularderie Island Historical Society (Rowlett owner entry); Acadia University (Lighthouse Friends visitor note). See notes.

events.note: Pole beacon established on McNeil Beach; fixed red light 33 ft above water, visible about eight miles (LF).
Lauchlin McNeil placed in charge 6 August 1884.
Pole light replaced by a 33-foot wooden tower; contract L. Mury of West Arichat, $780 (LF; Department report for fiscal 1909-10). NSLPS calls the 1909 work 'an alteration of some form'.
NSLPS dates a 6th-order dioptric lens to 1922, in operation 1930. The Department's report for fiscal 1909-10 already describes a 6th-order apparatus in the new tower.
Not operating 1955 to 1962 (NSLPS; Rowlett; Boularderie Island history). Lighthouse Friends dates the discontinuance to 1961.
Discontinued when the Seal Island Bridge was completed and lighted buoys marked the channel beneath it (LF).
Bought by a private owner for $250; one-storey addition built and later removed (LF; Rowlett). Boularderie Island history gives 1966 for private purchase and 'decommissioned' in 1965.
Donated by the owner to Acadia University; the university returned it to the owner for lack of long-term use (LF; Rowlett). Boularderie Island history gives 1996 for the donation.
Restored 2004 to 2005 with funds from the J.M. Kaplan Fund; floors and corner posts replaced (LF).
The owner died; the owner's daughter offered to donate the lighthouse to the Boularderie Island Historical Society (LF).

notes_for_editor: Ownership and access conflict. The Lighthouse Friends visitor note says 'owned by Acadia University', but its history says the university returned it to Bentley, and that his daughter 'has offered' to donate it to the Boularderie Island Historical Society. The Rowlett directory names the Historical Society as owner. The record's visit.climbable: true contradicts both sources (see corrections). The agency field is now written as disputed. Discontinuance: Lighthouse Friends dates it to the bridge's completion in 1961; NSLPS, Rowlett and the Boularderie Island history say the light was not operating 1955 to 1962. The story states both. Purchase and gift dates: 1965 (LF, NSLPS, Rowlett) vs 1966 purchase (BIHS); 1998 (LF, Rowlett) vs 1996 gift (BIHS). The story states both. The 1909 work: Department and Lighthouse Friends say the new tower replaced the pole; NSLPS and BIHS call it 'an alteration of some form'. Stated in the story and events. The sixth-order lens: the Department's 1909-10 report already describes a sixth-order apparatus; NSLPS dates a sixth-order dioptric lens to 1922, in operation 1930. Both stated. The 1884 appointment date comes from LF (6 August 1884). The Department's 1910-11 keepers' table has 'McNeil's Beach' with 'Aug. 6' and no legible year; the row was read from the OCR line, and the page image was not legible enough at the viewer's resolution to confirm it (scan p. 244 of 1912v46i14p21_0847). The 1903 list entry is on scan p. 231 (printed p. 218). Range: the 1909-10 report says 'five miles' with no unit stated, so the range_nm field was removed rather than recorded as nautical miles. Not checked: a current Canadian Coast Guard status (the light is not active); whether the Boularderie Island Historical Society or Acadia holds the title today.
